intent: Implement an optional secure node-local archive cache for Kubernetes scale-out
Build verified content storage and concurrent fill coordination

name: Node cache blob store
role: Stores verified content-addressed blobs in a private directory and coalesces concurrent fills in one process
conditions: Every caller must authorize access before calling the store; total disk limits, eviction, endpoint routing and service authentication remain unimplemented

subject: Cache integrity
why: Verify size and SHA-256 before atomic publication and on each hit; a partial or corrupt file must not reach the JVM

title: Use verified digest-addressed files and coordinate concurrent fills
why: Digest checks and atomic publication protect consumers while per-digest coordination avoids duplicate downloads in a burst
alternative: Independent per-request downloads and unverified files — rejected: they multiply transfers and can expose incomplete data

intent: Authorize node cache requests using Kubernetes identities and explicit grants

name: Node cache authorization
role: Validates service-account tokens through Kubernetes TokenReview and checks exact subject, registry and repository grants
conditions: Each request needs review and an explicit operator grant; the service endpoint and registry authorization are not implemented yet

subject: Token review audience
why: Reject reviews without the intended audience, reread the reviewer token for rotation, and never follow API redirects with credentials

title: Require token review and explicit repository grants for cache access
why: An authenticated identity must have an explicit grant before it can access shared private archive bytes
alternative: Anonymous node-local access — rejected: workloads on the same node could read each other's archives

intent: Partition cached content by registry and repository

name: Repository-scoped cache keys
role: Separates stored blobs and concurrent fills by exact registry, repository and content digest
conditions: The caller still needs an explicit repository grant and a miss must be obtained from that same repository

subject: Digest is not authorization
why: A digest-only hit could expose a blob cached from another private repository without checking access to it

title: Partition cache entries by repository and digest
why: The same digest in a different repository is a different authorization boundary
alternative: A global digest-only cache — rejected: an authorized caller for one repository could retrieve another repository's cached blob

intent: Require workload and registry authorization before serving a cache request

name: Node cache request handler
role: Requires TLS, reviews the workload identity, checks an explicit repository grant and invokes a separate registry verifier before any cache access
conditions: Registry verification and blob-source interfaces are not yet implemented for real registries; no server or pod integration is deployed

subject: Cached access after revocation
why: Registry authorization must be rechecked on every request, including hits, so an old cache entry cannot bypass changed permissions

title: Check both workload grant and registry access on every cache request
why: An operator grant alone does not prove that the caller still has registry permission for the blob
alternative: Trust service-account grants alone on cache hits — rejected: a revoked registry permission could be bypassed

intent: Verify current registry pull permission for cache hits

name: OCI registry permission verifier
role: Checks caller pull access to the exact repository blob on every request using a bounded range GET to an operator-allowed HTTPS registry
conditions: A direct 200 or 206 is required; redirected blob requests are denied for the cache path, and real registry compatibility is not yet tested

subject: Authorization on cache hits
why: Recheck current registry access rather than treating a prior successful cache fill as permanent permission

title: Recheck blob pull access at the registry without forwarding redirects
why: A small GET checks current access to the exact blob while keeping caller credentials on the configured registry origin
alternative: Trust cached authorization or forward credentials through redirects — rejected: revoked permissions or credential disclosure could expose archives

intent: Fetch cache misses from an allowed OCI repository

name: OCI registry blob source
role: Downloads an allowed repository's blob using a separate read-only credential loaded from a file for each miss
conditions: Only direct HTTPS responses are supported; redirects, automatic token exchange and deployment provisioning remain unimplemented

subject: Credential separation
why: The caller's current registry authorization is verified separately on every request; the shared fill uses the operator-controlled repository credential

title: Use a separate rotating-file source credential for cache misses
why: The operator controls shared download access without retaining a caller's registry credential for future fills
alternative: Use the first caller's credential for the shared fill — rejected: cache-fill availability would depend on that caller's credential and lifecycle

intent: Bound node cache payload and concurrent fills

name: Node cache capacity accounting
role: Counts existing cached payload and reserves space for each in-progress fill before downloading
conditions: The directory requires a single owning store process; limits exclude filesystem metadata, and eviction and automatic corrupt-entry removal are not implemented

subject: Concurrent disk use
why: Independent fills must reserve their expected sizes under one lock or together they can exceed the configured limit

title: Reserve cache capacity before each fill
why: A hard payload budget must include simultaneous temporary downloads as well as committed blobs
alternative: Check disk usage only after downloads or immediately delete in-use entries — rejected: concurrent fills could overrun the budget or disrupt readers

intent: Configure the authenticated TLS node cache service

name: Node cache service configuration
role: Builds the TLS server, Kubernetes token reviewer, registry verifier, repository source and bounded content store from explicit configuration
conditions: Configuration is internal; there is no runnable entry point or Kubernetes deployment yet, and eviction is not implemented

subject: Separate TLS trust
why: Kubernetes and registry credentials must only go to services whose certificates validate against the appropriate trust roots

title: Use explicit repository grants and separate TLS trust for service dependencies
why: The cache handles workload tokens and private archives, so its peer identities and allowed repositories must be explicit
alternative: Shared insecure or implicit trust — rejected: credentials could be sent to an unverified service

intent: Add a separate node cache executable

name: Node cache executable
role: Loads service configuration, starts the TLS cache server and drains requests during shutdown
conditions: The tools image carries the binary, but no Kubernetes workload or application fetch integration uses it yet

subject: Service lifecycle
why: A long-running node service needs bounded graceful shutdown independently of the application launcher

title: Ship the node cache as a separate executable
why: The optional long-running service has a lifecycle and configuration distinct from pod startup
alternative: Add the service as an application launcher subcommand — rejected: this couples service lifecycle and pod startup responsibilities

intent: Package a node-local cache service for Kubernetes

name: Node cache Helm chart
role: Runs a TLS cache DaemonSet with private pod storage, local-only Service routing and TokenReview permission
conditions: Requires Kubernetes 1.26 or later, an existing configuration Secret and a compatible image; the fetch client, direct fallback and eviction remain unimplemented

subject: Local Service routing
why: A node without a local cache endpoint has no endpoint for that Service and must use the direct registry path once the client fallback exists

title: Deploy a cache DaemonSet with local-only routing and pod-local storage
why: Each node can reuse its own cache without exposing or sharing host filesystem paths with workload pods
alternative: Use a node hostPath or cluster-wide Service — rejected: host access increases isolation risk and remote cache endpoints defeat node locality
